It correctly identifies very early on that the problem is unsolvable because the total number of eggs is unknown. However, instead of stating this conclusion and stopping, it repeatedly re-analyzes the problem, forms the same equations, and comes to the same conclusion over and over again, both within a single long turn and across subsequent turns. This is a classic example of step repetition and being unaware of the termination condition (i.e., stopping when a problem is deemed unsolvable). The agent also fails to ask for the missing information it has identified (the total number of eggs), which would be a productive way to handle the ambiguity.
